meta.title: PostgreSQL Database Design Documents
meta.description: DDD documentation framework for PostgreSQL database design projects. AI reads this file and generates .md files covering logical modeling, PG-specific physical design (extensions, partitioning, RLS, indexes), migration tooling, and operational readiness.
meta.applicable_when: Designing a new PostgreSQL database or refactoring an existing schema where the database is the primary deliverable — not a supporting component of a web app. Use when the project involves physical PG design decisions: index type selection (B-tree/GIN/GiST/BRIN), declarative partitioning, Row-Level Security, pg_audit, PITR, pgTAP testing, and zero-downtime DDL migrations. Distinct from ddd-web-app DATA_MODEL.md which treats the database as one of many components.

agent_instructions.role: You are a PostgreSQL database design documentation generator. Read this file and produce each document listed in phases[], in dependency order. Each document must reference content from its depends_on[] documents — do not generate generic content.
agent_instructions.generation_order_strategy: Topological sort by depends_on graph. Phase 1 (Requirements) has no upstream deps — generate first. Phase 2 (Logical Design) translates business requirements into a relational model. Phase 3 (Physical Design) maps the logical model to PostgreSQL-specific DDL, indexes, partitions, and security. Phase 4 (Operations) prepares for deployment, testing, and production. Never generate a Phase 3 document before its Phase 2 prerequisites are complete.
agent_instructions.content_language: Write narrative content in Thai. Use English for all identifiers, SQL, DDL, column names, table names, schema names, PostgreSQL extension names, index names, role names, function names, and technical jargon (B-tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, RLS, PITR, WAL, MVCC, TOAST, pgTAP, pg_audit, pg_stat_statements, pgBackRest). Preserve PG-specific terms in English even inside Thai sentences.
agent_instructions.quality_gate: Each document must cover all sections[] listed. Every table in SCHEMA_SPEC.md must trace back to an entity in ERD.md. Every column must have an entry in DATA_DICTIONARY.md. Every index in INDEXING_STRATEGY.md must reference a table in SCHEMA_SPEC.md and a query pattern in ACCESS_PATTERNS.md. Every RLS policy in SECURITY.md must name the actual role and table. Validate that all refs[] in sections resolve to real document IDs before writing.
domain_specific_notes: Database Design is not Web App design. There is no UI, no API layer, no deployment pipeline. The deliverable is a PostgreSQL schema — DDL scripts, migration files, and operational runbooks.

SCHEMA_SPEC.md is the equivalent of ARCHITECTURE.md in the web-app template. It is the single source of truth for the physical database structure including extensions, schemas, custom types, tables, constraints, triggers, and functions.

ACCESS_PATTERNS.md replaces the web-app PRD as the primary demand signal. Query patterns, hot paths, and read/write ratios drive every indexing and partitioning decision. Generate it before any physical design document.

The web-app DATA_MODEL.md expands into 4 separate documents here: DOMAIN_MODEL.md (business concepts), ERD.md (entity relationships), DATA_DICTIONARY.md (field-level canonical definitions), NORMALIZATION.md (design rationale and denormalization decisions).

INDEXING_STRATEGY.md is PostgreSQL-specific: use B-tree for equality/range, GIN for jsonb/array/tsvector/pg_trgm, GiST for geometry/range types/exclusion constraints, BRIN for append-only time-series tables, Hash for equality-only (rare). Always use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in production.

SECURITY.md focuses on PostgreSQL-native security: Row-Level Security (RLS) with USING/WITH CHECK policies, column-level GRANT/REVOKE, pg_audit configuration, pgcrypto for column-level encryption. Application-layer auth (JWT, OAuth) is out of scope.
TESTING_STRATEGY.md uses pgTAP as the primary framework — not pytest or Jest. pgTAP tests run inside PostgreSQL and can test constraints, triggers, functions, and RLS policies at the database level.

MIGRATION_STRATEGY.md covers zero-downtime DDL patterns specific to PostgreSQL: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (no table lock), ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN with DEFAULT (PG 11+ instant), safe NOT NULL addition, online column type changes via new-column-backfill-rename pattern.
Storage, IOPS, and connection pool capacity are the primary resource constraints — not cloud compute cost. Track these in CONSTRAINTS.md, not as an afterthought.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a CONSTRAINTS.md documenting all non-negotiable constraints. Cover: (1) PG major version + cloud provider (AWS RDS, Cloud SQL, Supabase, self-hosted) and required extensions; (2) scale projections — table row counts at 1yr/3yr, IOPS budget, storage budget, max concurrent connections; (3) PDPA compliance — data classification levels, retention periods, audit trail requirements, data subject rights; (4) HA/DR — RPO and RTO as numeric values, replication type, number of replicas; (5) budget and timeline. Every constraint must be stated as a testable, numeric requirement where possible.
agent_hints.input_context: Root document — no upstream dependencies. These constraints feed into every downstream design decision: PG version determines safe DDL patterns (MIGRATION_STRATEGY.md), scale determines partitioning candidates (PARTITIONING.md), PDPA drives column classification (SECURITY.md).
agent_hints.validation: Must specify PG major version. RPO and RTO must be numeric (e.g., RPO ≤ 5 min, RTO ≤ 30 min). PDPA section must define at least 3 sensitivity levels. Scale constraints must include row count projections for the largest table.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate an ACCESS_PATTERNS.md cataloging every significant query pattern against the database. For each pattern provide: query name, SQL sketch or pseudocode, frequency (QPS or daily count), p99 latency SLA, and columns used in WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY. Identify the top 5-10 hot paths — the most frequent or most latency-sensitive queries that drive index and partition design. Document per-table read/write ratios and write patterns (bulk inserts, upserts, batch deletes). This document is the primary input for INDEXING_STRATEGY.md and PARTITIONING.md.
agent_hints.input_context: Derive query patterns from STAKEHOLDERS.md application consumers — each application's critical queries must appear here. Every query pattern listed will be used in INDEXING_STRATEGY.md to justify index selection.
agent_hints.validation: Every hot path must have a latency SLA. Read/write ratio must be provided for every major table. Write patterns must specify isolation level requirements (READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, SERIALIZABLE). At least 5 query patterns must be documented.

If inheritance exists, document the chosen PostgreSQL pattern: single-table with discriminator column, table-per-type with FK to parent, or partitioned inheritance — include trade-off rationale. Reference CONSTRAINTS.md PG version for each pattern's availability. Every migration must have a documented rollback procedure.
agent_hints.input_context: DDL from SCHEMA_SPEC.md defines what to migrate. PG version from CONSTRAINTS.md determines which DDL patterns are safe and available (PG 11+ instant ADD COLUMN, PG 14+ DETACH PARTITION CONCURRENTLY).
